answer.answer: Neither. ST-EVA holds no price-to-sales ratio for AAPL. There is no metric named "current_ps" in the database: the query was refused as an unknown metric, and the metrics ST-EVA knows are assets, capex, cash, debt, dividend_per_share, eps_diluted, gross_profit, guidance, income_tax, interest_expense, long_term_debt_current, long_term_debt_noncurrent, net_income, operating_cash_flow, operating_income, operating_margin_bank, r_and_d, revenue, sbc, segment_revenue, sga and shares_outstanding. The AAPL coverage report lists 12 metrics held, none of them a valuation ratio. So there is no figure that was either reported by a source or calculated by ST-EVA, and no operands of a calculation exist to name. One input a price-to-sales ratio would require, revenue, is held for AAPL in a SOURCE_REPORTED state (339 observations), and shares_outstanding is held as SOURCE_REPORTED (72 observations), but no price series is among the known metrics, so no ratio could be assembled from what is here. This is a different situation from a figure that exists and is in a negative state: no observation was returned because no such concept is held, and a query for a metric that does exist but lacks rows for a period would look the same. I have cited no observation ids, because none were returned for a current price-to-sales figure.
uncertainties: ST-EVA holds no current P/S (price-to-sales) observation for AAPL, so whether such a figure was reported or calculated cannot be answered from this evidence either way.
No price or market-capitalisation metric appears among the metrics ST-EVA knows, so even the components of a price-to-sales ratio are not all available here.

Revenue (339 observations) and shares_outstanding (72 observations) are held for AAPL as SOURCE_REPORTED, but their periods and units were not retrieved, so they cannot be used to characterise any ratio.
